headers: Why the Limit is Set This Way
cells: Dry, brittle, powder-like, or pliable materials.
Chalk, wax crayons, modeling clay, compressed paint tablets, colored pencil cores, dry pastels.
High ingestion risk, but lower surface-area-to-volume ratio for rapid leaching compared to liquids.

headers: Why the Limit is Set This Way
cells: Finger paints, liquid tempera, slime, liquid ink in pens, bubble solution, glue sticks, wet modeling dough.
STRICTEST LIMITS. Highest risk because liquids are swallowed easily and elements are already in a highly bioavailable state.

headers: Why the Limit is Set This Way
cells: Painted wood, printed cardboard, coated plastic toys, metallic finishes, laminated surfaces.
Tested by physically scraping the coating off the base material. Limits are higher because the total mass of the coating is small.
